novelty.justification: The claim proposes that scientific foundation models encode laws such that "a scalar physical input maps monotonically and log-linearly onto a low-dimensional representational axis whose slope recovers the true scaling exponent," supplemented by a test of whether dimensionally equivalent variables share an axis; its novelty route is therefore a quantitative representation measurement rather than merely a new scientific setting. Searches using "latent representation physical scaling exponent probe," "neural network internal inverse square law linear probe," and "dimensional consistency foundation model representations" identify the closest work as The Observer Effect in World Models: Invasive Adaptation Corrupts Latent Physics (2026), whose PhyIP protocol already uses frozen low-capacity probes to recover physical quantities and Newtonian inverse-square scaling, while Sparse Probes and Murky Physics (2026) likewise compares scientific-model internals with known physics. Moving from those studies to calibrated exponent-error scoring across many laws and shared subspaces for equal-dimensional variables is a substantive natural extension and new operationalization, but not a new core interpretability paradigm, supporting standard rather than high novelty.
